title: District shapes can be measured for mischief
body: The efficiency gap and compactness scores turn gerrymandering into geometry: measure how many votes each side wastes, or how tentacled a district's perimeter is versus its area. Courts have entertained Polsby-Popper scores, perimeter squared over area, as evidence. Democracy's fairness arguments now include fractal-adjacent shape forensics, which would have delighted and alarmed the 1812 cartoonists who named the practice.
